8 Best Restaurants to Try in Akumal

Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:56
Instaread

Akumal may be best known for its sea turtles and laid-back Caribbean beaches, but the town also has an impressive dining scene that’s well worth exploring. From casual beachfront taco shacks to upscale restaurants serving fresh seafood and wood-fired pizzas, there’s something here for every appetite and budget.

Many of Akumal’s restaurants emphasize locally caught fish, authentic Mexican flavors, and open-air dining that lets you soak up the tropical atmosphere long after the sun goes down.

Whether you’re fueling up with breakfast before snorkeling in Akumal Bay, grabbing a leisurely lunch with an ocean view, or settling in for a romantic dinner under the stars, you’ll find plenty of memorable places to eat.

If you’re wondering where to eat during your stay, these are the 8 restaurants that consistently deliver great food, friendly service, and an authentic taste of Akumal.

1. Lol-Ha Restaurant

Photo Credit: Macca Sherifi

  • Location: Akumal Beach
  • Cuisine: Mexican seafood, international
  • Best for: Lunch with a view, casual dinners, reliable first-day dining

Lol-Ha sits directly on the sand at Akumal Bay, with open-air palapa dining and one of the best views of the turtle bay on the coast. The relaxed beachfront atmosphere makes it a favorite stop after a morning snorkeling trip, and the combination of ocean breezes, cold drinks, and Caribbean scenery captures the essence of an Akumal vacation.

Go for grilled whole fish, fresh ceviche, or one of the Yucatecan preparations bursting with achiote and citrus. The setting does a lot of the work, but the food holds up, with generous portions and classic regional flavors that showcase the area’s coastal ingredients.

This is the most iconic restaurant in town, which also makes it the busiest. Reservations aren’t accepted, and tables fill quickly at lunch. If you’re visiting during high season, aim to arrive early or be prepared to wait. The best tables are those closest to the beach, where you can watch the waves roll in while enjoying a leisurely meal.

2. La Buena Vida Restaurant & Bar

  • Location: Half Moon Bay
  • Cuisine: Seafood, Mexican, bar food
  • Best for: Casual beach lunches, sunset drinks, the swing-seat bar experience

La Buena Vida is one of the best-reviewed restaurants in Akumal and the one most likely to come up if you ask a repeat visitor where to eat. The swing seats at the beach bar are the signature detail, and the combination of fresh fish, cold drinks, and a relaxed atmosphere keeps the place consistently full.

The kitchen does classic dishes very well; you can expect fish tacos, the fresh catch of the day, and shrimp dishes prepared simply with good ingredients.

The bar is a strong draw on its own, and it’s the kind of place where a quick afternoon drink turns into an evening out.

3. Taverna Akumal

  • Location: Plaza Ukana
  • Cuisine: Northern Italian
  • Best for: Dinners, date nights, a break from seafood

Taverna Akumal is an Italian restaurant in Plaza Ukana that draws a loyal crowd with its wood-fired pizza and handmade pasta. It’s the strongest non-seafood option in town and one of the most consistent kitchens on the Akumal restaurant strip.

The environment is warm and comfortable, the service is attentive, and the menu reads like a genuine northern Italian trattoria rather than a beach town approximation of one.

his is the spot to bookmark if your group is in the mood for European cuisine and a break from fresh seafood and local flavors. Reservations are worth making during the high season.

4. Taquería La Lunita

Photo Credit: Teri Virbickis

  • Location: Across Highway 307
  • Cuisine: Seafood, Mexican
  • Best for: Relaxed breakfasts, lunches, fresh tacos

Taquería La Lunita is a quieter, more local-feeling alternative to the tourist hotspots of Lol-Ha and La Buena Vida. The menu offers fresh juices and flavorful tacos, service is relaxed and friendly, and dishes are generous and affordable.

This spot is popular with visitors who have been to Akumal before and want something a step removed from the beachfront tourist circuit. Set your alarm because Taquería La Lunita opens early and closes at 2 pm.

5. Turtle Bay Bakery & Cafe

  • Location: Akumal town center
  • Cuisine: Cafe, breakfast, baked goods
  • Best for: Breakfast, coffee, morning fuel before snorkeling

Turtle Bay Bakery & Cafe is the best morning stop in Akumal. This small, casual spot is known for its baked goods, smoothie bowls, egg dishes, and strong coffee, but its lunches and dinners are equally delicious.

This isn’t a place for a long sit-down meal, and the menu is light and well-suited to the pace of an active morning. So, if you’re heading to the beach early to catch the turtles before the crowds arrive, this is where to start your day.

Lines can form on busy mornings, so plan accordingly.

6. La Cueva del Pescador

  • Location: Akumal town center
  • Cuisine: Seafood, Mexican
  • Best for: Budget-friendly fresh fish, local atmosphere, no-fuss dining

La Cueva del Pescador is among the most straightforwardly local options on this list. It’s casual, unpretentious, and known for fresh, simple dishes done well.

The prices are lower than at many beachfront spots, the portions are solid, and the clientele skews toward locals and repeat visitors who have moved past the main tourist drag.

If you want grilled fish without the markup that comes with a beachfront table, this is the place. 

7. Jungle Cafe

  • Location: Half Moon Bay
  • Cuisine: Local and international favorites
  • Best for: Chilaquiles and the cochinita pibil special

Jungle Cafe is a favorite breakfast and brunch spot known for its relaxed atmosphere, excellent coffee, and fresh, flavorful cuisine. With friendly service, healthy menu options, and a unique jungle-inspired ambiance just steps from the beach, this spot is a must-visit for anyone exploring Akumal.

Set beside a lush mangrove and decorated with colorful local artwork, Jungle Cafe offers a tranquil setting where guests can enjoy everything from chilaquiles and homemade quiche to French toast with house-made preserves and fresh smoothies.

Coffee lovers appreciate the menu of expertly crafted drinks, while weekend visitors often come early for the popular cochinita pibil special.

8. Surf Cowboy Grill & Bar

Photo Credit: Yalcin Sonat

  • Location: North Beach Road
  • Cuisine: Mexican, grilled meats
  • Best for: Cold drinks, watching sport, evening wind-down after the beach

Located along North Beach Road in Akumal, Surf Cowboy Grill & Bar is a laid-back restaurant and sports bar that combines casual Caribbean charm with hearty comfort food and friendly hospitality.

The menu features a mix of Mexican favorites, grilled specialties, burgers, seafood, fresh salads, and creative cocktails, making it a great choice for lunch, dinner, or sunset drinks after a day at the beach.

Guests appreciate the spacious, open-air atmosphere, attentive service, and relaxed vibe, with multiple TVs for watching live sports, a pool table, and daily happy-hour specials that add to the fun.

Which Akumal Restaurant Will You Try First?

Akumal’s food scene is small enough that you can cover most of it in a long weekend, and the quality across the board is better than the town’s size would suggest.

Lol-Ha and La Buena Vida are the anchors that most visitors hit on their first trip, but the quieter spots like Taqueria La Lunita and Turtle Bay Bakery are the ones they come back for.

For everything else worth planning before your trip, our guide to the best things to do in Akumal has you covered. If you’re still working out where to stay, our roundup of 12 incredible all-inclusive resorts in Akumal and our guide to 7 must-visit Akumal beaches are a good place to start.
